title: Building Holographic Entanglement by Measurement
topic: Holographic entanglement / tensor network / quantum hardware preparation
summary: Proposes a framework for preparing quantum states with holographic entanglement structure (obeying the Ryu-Takayanagi formula for a chosen bulk geometry) using only measurement-based operations. The bulk geometry is discretized into a coupling graph; evolving under this graph and measuring bulk nodes yields the desired boundary state. Works for hyperbolic disk and wormhole geometries. Requires only Gaussian operations + measurements -- implementable on photonic and cold-atom platforms.
key_findings: Measurement-based preparation of RT-formula-obeying entanglement for arbitrary chosen bulk geometries
Only Gaussian operations and measurements required -- hardware-efficient
Demonstrated numerically for hyperbolic disk and wormhole geometries
Does not require solving Einstein equations -- geometry is an input, not an output
project_relevance: WATCH. Complementary approach to MERA for preparing holographic states. Their measurement-based preparation is hardware-efficient (Gaussian + measurement) vs our VQE approach. The hyperbolic geometry they target is the same geometry our MERA lives in. Not directly competing -- they aim at state preparation, we aim at probing emergent forces. Monitor for any future work on force measurements in their framework.
competition_assessment: Not competing. Different goal (state preparation vs force measurement). Different platform (photonic/cold-atom vs trapped-ion/superconducting).
